text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Police have arrested 17 people including 11 civil servants in northern Kelantan state involved in the smuggling in and extortion of foreign workers, said Deputy Home Affairs Minister Megat Junid.
-- Malaysia's over-the-counter market is expected to be operational by the year's end, said Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
-- There were grounds for further investigations into alleged discrepancies in the award of an equipment-supply contract by Telekom Malaysia to Swedish firm LM Ericcson, said Deputy PM Anwar.
-- Three people were missing and 19 rescued when cargo vessel Rajah Mas sank in Sarawak.
-- A computer hacker broke into Internet service provider TMNet's system on Tuesday and altered its corporate homepage. The service is provided by Telekom Malaysia.
-- Plantations and food products firm Hap Seng Consolidated plans to invest one billion ringgit in the next five years in an aggressive expansion plan, said its chief executive John Madsen.
